learning_objective: 🎯 Learn how organizations peek into the future, set concrete objectives, and map out the absolute best course of action to achieve their goals!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Planning is deciding in advance what to do, how to do it, when to do it, and who is to do it. It bridges the gap between where we are and where we want to go.
It focuses on achieving objectives, is a primary function (precedes all other functions), is pervasive, continuous, futuristic (forward-looking), and involves decision-making.
Planning creates rigidity, may not work well in a highly dynamic environment, reduces employee creativity, involves huge costs, and is a very time-consuming process.
1. Setting Objectives -> 2. Developing Premises -> 3. Identifying Alternatives -> 4. Evaluating Alternatives -> 5. Selecting an Alternative -> 6. Implementing the Plan -> 7. Follow-up.
Plans can be 'Single-use' (Budgets, Programmes for a one-time event) or 'Standing plans' (Policies, Procedures, Rules that are used repeatedly).

fun_activity.title: 🏕️ The Ultimate Trip Planner
fun_activity.instructions: Plan a 3-day school trip to the mountains! You must define the objective, set the budget, create a step-by-step itinerary (procedure), and establish one strict safety rule for everyone to follow.

exam_tips: 📌 You MUST write the steps of the 'Planning Process' in exactly the correct sequence. Do not mix up the order!
📌 Planning does not guarantee success. Just because a plan worked in the past doesn't mean it will work in the future.
📌 Distinguish clearly between a 'Rule' (strict, no flexibility, e.g., No smoking) and a 'Policy' (general guideline, e.g., We only hire graduates).
quick_recap: ⭐ Planning is looking ahead, while controlling is looking back.
⭐ Premises are the assumptions made about the future on which the plan is built.
⭐ Even with the best planning, unforeseen environmental changes can derail an organization's goals.
